note: The fuzzer-controlled bytes are written verbatim into a temporary capture file, making the input bytes the source of the later parse path.
The temporary file is reopened through the capture-file reader selection logic, carrying the attacker-controlled bytes into the parser.
The reader obtains a packet header whose captured length governs the subsequent copy size.
The implementation copies pkthdr.caplen bytes from the packet buffer; malformed capture metadata can make this read exceed the allocated source buffer and trigger the heap-buffer-overflow read.
